- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.36 to +1.25); model tends to overshoot into next period.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -1.28 to -1.48), particularly in early periods of the 30-day horizon.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overreacts to short-term sentiment swings, then corrects too aggressively in subsequent periods.
- Forecast lags sentiment shifts: when sentiment turns negative mid-period, model doesn’t adjust downward until 2–3 days later.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overpredicts by 0.5–2.5% in the first 5–7 days, then converges — adjust downward early if sentiment is negative.
- When sentiment is consistently positive (e.g., 0.36–0.46), model tends to overfit upward momentum; reduce forecast slope after 3–5 days of positive sentiment.
- Avoid extrapolating sentiment trends beyond 3–5 days — sentiment decay or reversal often occurs within 7–10 days, so model should cap forecast growth after that.
